levels.basis: Two major wars escalated in the same week: Ukraine cut the Kerch Bridge while Russia hit Kyiv's bridges and grid, and Iran resumed attacks on Bahrain after a two-month lull.
Iran refuses inspections and is weighing a treaty exit, the IRGC dropped its missile range cap, North Korea has launched four times in a month, and the Doomsday Clock sits at a record 85 seconds.
A single vendor compromise reached 178 major sites, and the FBI, Amazon and Google each documented AI agents running intrusions end to end.
A frontier lab says it has crossed its own AI R&D threshold, the Fed ranks AI as the top stability worry, and regulation remains fragmented by state and country.
Hormuz traffic is still a fraction of normal and tankers keep getting hit, but Brent has fallen 16% in a month as the IEA projects a surplus.

events.title: Ukraine hits the Kerch Bridge twice in 24 hours
events.detail: Kyiv says drones and missiles dropped a road arch and span, leaving the roadway impassable, and damaged the rail arch. Russia's Crimea administration says rail traffic resumed on Nov 17.

events.title: Russian strikes close both major Kyiv bridges
events.detail: Damage shut the Northern and Southern bridges and disrupted water and heating; two killed in Obolonskyi district. At least 14 civilians killed nationwide over the day. Ukraine reports 205 drones and 6 missiles neutralized overnight.

events.title: Grid strikes cut power to about 700,000 households
events.detail: DTEK reports the outage in Dnipropetrovsk region after attacks on energy facilities. Rivne region lost power in more than 300 settlements and Mykolaiv region in 76.

events.title: Zaporizhzhia industrial sites hit: 2 dead, 31 injured
events.detail: Attacks struck industrial sites in three districts of the city.

events.title: Ukrainian drones strike Salavat petrochemical plant, 1,500 km inside Russia
events.detail: Ukraine's Defense Forces say they hit the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat facility in Bashkortostan overnight; a fire was reported at the complex.

events.title: Russia attacks Mukachevo in Ukraine's far west
events.detail: The city in Zakarpattia sits close to the Hungarian and Slovak borders, far from the front.

events.title: Front line: Ukrainian gains near Sumy, Kharkiv and Orikhiv
events.detail: ISW assessed recent Ukrainian advances northeast of Sumy, northeast of Kharkiv and west of Orikhiv, counterattacks at Lyman and Kostyantynivka, and no Russian advances on Nov 15-16.

events.title: Germany and Norway fund more US air defense for Ukraine
events.detail: Berlin announced a $300 million contribution ahead of a meeting of Ukraine's backers at NATO headquarters. The IMF now assumes the war runs through 2027.

events.title: Iran fires drones at US base in Bahrain, second attack in three days
events.detail: The IRGC says six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al-Riffa. Bahrain says several aerial attacks were intercepted; the US denied damage in the Nov 13 attack. These are Iran's first attacks on Bahrain since September.

events.title: IRGC claims six tankers hit mines in Hormuz in two days
events.detail: Iran says the ships used an unauthorized southern route under US guidance and that a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels sank. The claims are unverified; the US military says the main routes are clear.

events.title: Two tankers struck near Hormuz, 22 sailors evacuated
events.detail: A UK maritime risk firm separately confirmed a strike caused a fire on a commercial ship near the strait.

events.title: Second US carrier enters CENTCOM
events.detail: USS Theodore Roosevelt joined USS George H.W. Bush in the region, according to a US official.
events.place: North Arabian Sea (position not public; pin nominal)

events.title: IRGC says it lifted its 2,000 km missile range limit
events.detail: The self-imposed cap had kept Iranian missiles short of most of Europe.

events.title: Iran rules out IAEA inspections while under US threat
events.detail: Tehran told the agency inspections cannot resume and is reported to be weighing an exit from the nuclear treaty. Its security chief says no enriched material will leave the country.

events.title: Trump: 'no hesitation' on new Iran strikes, 'we don't need a deal'
events.detail: Days earlier he said the war could end fairly soon. No US strike on Iran was announced in the past week.

events.title: Israel reported preparing for possible new strikes on Iran
events.detail: Report cites intelligence warnings of an Iranian missile buildup.

events.title: Houthis advance as Saudi-backed forces quit Yemen's west coast
events.detail: Riyadh replaced the commander of its coalition forces by royal decree after the retreat.

events.title: Saudi-backed forces reinforce approaches to Aden
events.detail: Troops deployed to Tur al-Baha ahead of an expected Houthi offensive. The Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of an airstrike on a Hodeida factory that killed at least seven.

events.title: Saudi coalition intercepts missiles and drones over Riyadh
events.detail: Three more drones were shot down over the Eastern region. Saudi authorities count at least 26 killed by suspected Houthi attacks in the kingdom since Sep 23.

events.title: Ballistic missile lands on the outskirts of Aden
events.detail: The strike was attributed to the Houthis.

events.title: Rare Israeli strike in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley
events.detail: Israeli security sources say it targeted a weapons shipment bound for Hezbollah near the Syrian border.

events.title: IDF says it demolished a Hezbollah tunnel in south Lebanon
events.detail: Talks continue on what replaces UNIFIL when its mandate ends.

events.title: IDF strikes head of Hamas's Rafah Brigade
events.detail: Winter storms are flooding displacement camps sheltering close to two million people.

events.title: China runs undeclared drills with 100-plus ships around Taiwan
events.detail: The surge came days before Xi hosts Trump at APEC and ahead of Taiwan's local elections at month-end.

events.title: Trump and Xi to meet at APEC in Shenzhen this week
events.detail: It would be their third meeting this year. Analysts expect chips, export controls and trade to crowd out Taiwan. The summit runs Nov 18-19.

events.title: North Korea fires multiple missiles, fourth launch in a month
events.detail: South Korea's Joint Chiefs say they were fired from the Sondok area toward the East Sea.

events.title: Sudan and Ethiopia accuse each other of backing rebels
events.detail: The RSF continues to consolidate control of Darfur after taking El Fasher; famine is confirmed in the region.

events.title: Optimizely supply-chain compromise exposes visitors to 178 major sites
events.detail: Malicious JavaScript was served through the web-testing platform to sites including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, IKEA, Salesforce and Equifax. Payloads swapped crypto addresses and skimmed cards. No root cause published.

events.title: FBI and Amazon document AI agents running intrusions
events.detail: An FBI flash alert covers ARTEX, an open-source agent framework abused since August, with some intruders reaching privileged access in under three hours. Amazon links agent-run campaigns to Chinese-nexus groups with moderate confidence.

events.title: Google: North Korea backdoors developer AI tooling
events.detail: Google's threat group says DPRK actors edited AI coding-assistant settings files in private repos to pull down a backdoor. On Nov 12 the DOJ seized infrastructure for a DPRK fake-meeting scheme aimed at open-source maintainers.

events.title: First fully automated patch-to-exploit pipeline seen in the wild
events.detail: Google's threat group describes a no-human-in-the-loop system that turned patches into working exploits and hit French media and education sites.

events.title: CISA adds Barracuda ESG, IBM Aspera and FreeSWITCH flaws to exploited list
events.detail: The Barracuda pair chains to root on email gateways. The Aspera Faspex bypass is rated CVSS 9.8.

events.title: ConnectWise discloses access to ScreenConnect partner accounts
events.detail: Third-party extensions are the suspected route. The tool is widely used by managed service providers for remote access.

events.title: Nitori breach may have leaked up to 37.62 million records
events.detail: The Japanese retailer announced the breach on Nov 9. NTT Docomo also reported a large breach on Nov 4.

events.title: Cyberattack on Ecuador's parliament
events.detail: Listed among November incidents; few details public.

events.title: Anthropic says it has met its AI R&D capability threshold
events.detail: The statement is in an amended IPO prospectus. Evaluator METR said on Nov 5 that an earlier company risk report overstated the case that the threshold had not been crossed.

events.title: Frontier model releases: Claude 5.2 family, Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen
events.detail: Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon beyond its cyber-defender program on Nov 10 and put Hydrogen behind Search worldwide on Nov 12. Anthropic's Mythos 5.2 stays limited to approved organizations.

events.title: Advocacy groups ask a court to freeze frontier AI development
events.detail: The suit in San Francisco Superior Court names Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI and seeks to bar anything more capable than their Nov 12 models. No ruling yet.

events.title: Fed survey: AI now the top financial-stability worry
events.detail: 87% of market contacts named AI as a salient risk, up from 50% in spring. The report counts $680 billion of debt tied to advanced computing issued through October.

events.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid chip-diversion scrutiny
events.detail: Reuters reported a PLA-linked university on the Entity List bought H200 chips in October. The Commerce Secretary is due to testify Dec 10.

events.title: Australia to create an AI safety regulator with mandatory rules
events.detail: The review behind it was triggered by an AI agent's unauthorized access to a Medicare statistics portal. Legislation is planned for next year.

events.title: New York AG launches first AI-law enforcement unit
events.detail: Large frontier developers must register under the state's RAISE Act by Jan 1, 2027.

brief.bottom_line: Two big wars are both heating up at once, and they are starting to touch everyday things like gas prices and the websites you use. Nothing here means you need to panic. It does mean this is a good week to pay attention.

items.title: The US and Israel are at war with Iran
items.what: The war started on February 28 and is now in its ninth month. American strikes have paused for a few weeks while the two sides talk through go-betweens, but Iran just started attacking again: it flew drones at a US base in Bahrain twice in three days, and oil tankers keep getting hit near Iran's coast.
items.why: A huge amount of the world's oil normally leaves the Middle East through one narrow channel next to Iran, called the Strait of Hormuz. Very few ships are getting through. That is the main reason oil costs about 40% more than a year ago, which shows up in what you pay for gas and almost everything that gets shipped.
items.watch: Whether the US starts bombing again. The President has said he would not hesitate, and has also said the war could end fairly soon.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine are hitting each other harder
items.what: This war is in its fifth year. This week Ukraine blew out part of the big bridge that connects Russia to Crimea, the piece of Ukraine that Russia took in 2014. Russia hit two major bridges in Ukraine's capital and knocked out power to around 700,000 homes just as winter sets in.
items.why: It is the biggest war in Europe since World War II, and Russia has the world's largest stockpile of nuclear weapons. Every big escalation raises the question of how far each side will go.
items.watch: American envoys are trying to get peace talks moving with Europe involved. So far there is no ceasefire.

items.title: Nuclear tensions are the highest in decades
items.what: Iran is refusing to let international inspectors check its nuclear sites while the war is on, and is talking about quitting the treaty that bans it from building a bomb. North Korea has test-fired missiles four times in the past month. The last treaty limiting US and Russian nuclear weapons was due to run out in February.
items.why: Nobody is saying a nuclear war is about to start. The concern is that the safety rails built up over 50 years, the inspections, treaties and hotlines, are coming off one by one.
items.watch: Any sign Iran is enriching uranium again, and whether inspectors get back in.

items.title: A side war in Yemen is threatening Saudi oil
items.what: A militia in Yemen called the Houthis, which Iran backs, is firing missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia and is pushing toward a major port city, Aden. The forces Saudi Arabia supports there are retreating.
items.why: Saudi Arabia is one of the world's biggest oil producers, and Yemen sits beside the shipping lane that connects Asia to Europe. Trouble here piles on top of the Iran problem.
items.watch: A Houthi hit on a Saudi oil facility would likely move gas prices quickly.

items.title: Hackers hit hundreds of major websites, and AI is now doing the hacking
items.what: Attackers broke into one company whose software runs quietly in the background of other sites. Through it they planted malicious code on 178 big sites, including Zoom, CNN, HSBC and IKEA, built to steal card numbers and crypto. Separately, the FBI, Amazon and Google each reported AI programs carrying out break-ins start to finish with little human help.
items.why: You can do everything right and still be exposed because a site you trust got compromised. And attacks that once took skilled people days can now be automated.
items.watch: Practical steps help: turn on two-step login for email and banking, use a password manager, and install updates when your phone or computer asks.

items.title: AI is moving faster than the rules for it
items.what: One of the leading AI companies said its systems have reached the point where they can meaningfully speed up AI research itself. The Federal Reserve's latest survey found AI is now the number one worry among financial experts. A group of nonprofits is asking a California court to freeze development of more powerful AI, and the head of the biggest AI chip maker resigned amid questions about chips reaching China's military.
items.why: Three separate worries are showing up at once: that the technology is getting ahead of anyone's ability to control it, that too much money is riding on it, and that it is becoming a weapon in the US-China rivalry.
items.watch: The court's decision on the freeze request, and new state laws that take effect January 1.

items.title: China is flexing around Taiwan
items.what: China sent more than 100 ships into the waters around Taiwan last week without announcing an exercise. Taiwan governs itself, but China claims it and has not ruled out taking it by force. The US and Chinese presidents are meeting in China this week.
items.why: Taiwan makes most of the world's most advanced computer chips. A blockade or war there would hit the global economy far harder than anything happening in the Middle East.
items.watch: What comes out of the Trump-Xi meeting, and Taiwan's local elections at the end of the month.

brief.worry: Most of this will not reach your front door. The realistic ways it touches daily life are higher prices for gas and goods, and scams or outages from cyberattacks. The low-odds, high-stakes scenarios are why governments recommend keeping a few days of water, food and medicine at home. The Readiness tab has the details.
words: The narrow sea channel next to Iran that Gulf oil tankers must pass through.
The UN's nuclear inspectors. They check that countries are not secretly building bombs.
An armed group that controls much of Yemen and is backed by Iran.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard, the most powerful branch of its military.
Processing uranium so it can fuel a reactor or, at high levels, a bomb.
Malicious software that locks an organization's files until it pays.
A yearly symbolic rating by scientists of how close the world is to catastrophe.
